slides.title: A breath changes the cue.
items: When a singer holds a note, the translation must wait. An operator follows the performance, watches the conductor and releases one prepared line at a time.

slides.title: From the last row
items: A single translation sits above the action. The operator clears it when the singer finishes the phrase.

slides.title: A human has the button
items: The stage manager approves the running order. The operator rehearses the triggers and sees the current and next lines at once.
If the cast skips ahead, the operator can jump to a cue or clear the display. A local copy travels with the touring company.

slides.title: Book once for the tour
items: Covers script import, one approved language track and a technical rehearsal with the house operator.
A ten-show run would invoice $3,000. Additional translation is quoted separately.

slides.title: The first buyer is a touring producer
items: A company translating the same production for multiple houses already has approved text. Its producer buys the setup; each venue receives a display test and handover.
Planning case: 40 producers × 3 tours × $3,000 yields $360,000 in annual bookings at full adoption.

slides.title: What a rehearsal can prove
items: Cue edits carried into opening night, illustrative test
Compare two runs of the same excerpt. Count missed, late and incorrect lines from the stage manager’s annotated score. The figures illustrate the pilot method.

slides.title: The alternatives on the desk
items: Easy to prepare. A last-minute cut means checking slide order and the operator’s separate notes.
A strong fit for resident companies. A tour must confirm what every host can import and display.
The company carries a reviewed cue file and a local playback copy. Every host signs off on the same excerpt.

slides.title: Two desks, one sign-off
items: Ada owns translations, approvals and line breaks. She signs off on readability from the last row before the first paid performance.
Eli owns playback and recovery. Every tour leaves rehearsal with a tested spare machine and an operator who has practiced a restart.

slides.title: Before the curtain rises
items: Commission three paid productions and test the same scene from three seating positions.
Complete thirty shows. Log every manual recovery and rehearse the common failure modes again.
Secure two repeat bookings and publish a standard venue handover packet.

slides.title: Hold for opening night.
items: $330k for local playback, $240k for tour onboarding and $180k for rehearsal support. The 15-month target is thirty performances and two repeat producers.
